ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: on the cell membrane there is a transmembrane G-protein-linked receptor (GPCR), and on the extracellular side the ligand epinephrine binds to this receptor; on the inner side of the membrane, the receptor is connected to a G protein containing α, β, and γ subunits, and involves GDP/GTP exchange; subsequently the α subunit carrying GTP interacts with adenylyl cyclase, causing ATP to be converted into cAMP, further activating downstream cAMP-dependent protein kinase. It can be seen from this that the role of this GPCR setup is to transmit the extracellular ligand signal that cannot directly enter the cell into the cell. If a certain ligand itself can pass through the lipid bilayer cell membrane, then a membrane receptor is not needed to recognize it on the outside and relay it into the cell through the G protein. The typical property of being able to pass through the cell membrane on its own is that the molecule is small and nonpolar/lipid-soluble.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: an extracellular ligand binds a membrane-spanning GPCR, which communicates across the lipid bilayer to intracellular G protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and downstream kinase. From the text, note the question asks when such a membrane receptor setup would be unnecessary. Apply the rule that if a ligand can cross the plasma membrane by itself, it does not need an external receptor-to-internal relay. Therefore the ligand property is being small and nonpolar/lipid-soluble.
method.CoT_raw: 图像显示：细胞膜上有一个跨膜的G-protein-linked receptor（GPCR），细胞外侧有配体 epinephrine 与该受体结合；受体在膜内侧与含 α、β、γ 亚基的 G 蛋白相连，并涉及 GDP/GTP 交换；随后 α 亚基携带 GTP 与腺苷酸环化酶（adenylyl cyclase）相互作用，使 ATP 转化为 cAMP，进一步激活下游 cAMP 依赖性蛋白激酶。由此可见，这种GPCR设置的作用是把不能直接进入细胞的细胞外配体信号传递到细胞内。如果某种配体本身可以穿过脂质双层细胞膜，就不需要膜受体在外侧识别并通过G蛋白 relay 到细胞内。能自行通过细胞膜的典型性质是分子小且非极性/脂溶性。
method.model_answer: 配体是小的非极性分子（脂溶性、能直接穿过细胞膜）时，像GPCR这样的膜受体设置是不必要的。
method.answer_match_reason: 预测答案明确指出配体是“小的非极性分子”，并补充说明其脂溶性、能直接穿过细胞膜，这与标准答案含义一致。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as showing epinephrine ligand outside the cell binding a G-protein-linked receptor spanning the membrane; the receptor activates intracellular G protein, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and kinase signaling, demonstrating that the receptor bridges a ligand that remains extracellular to intracellular effects.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use membrane permeability principles: small nonpolar molecules can diffuse through the hydrophobic lipid bilayer and bind intracellular targets directly, whereas large or polar/charged ligands need surface receptors such as GPCRs to transmit signals across the membrane.
